primary_issue: Severe underexposure + no readable flame subject (no visible blue core/yellow body/wick), compounded by extreme/unfocused DOF—image is mostly indistinct dark blobs.
issues: Scene is dramatically underexposed; primary subject (candle/flame) is effectively invisible.
No convincing candle-flame structure: missing sharp teardrop silhouette, blue-white inner cone near wick, and yellow→orange outer flame gradient.
Wick/candle top not readable, so scale and contact point for flame are lost.
Smoke (if present) reads as thick amorphous volume rather than thin wisps/filaments; lacks high-frequency detail.
Lighting does not sell the flame as the sole light source: brass/wax/desk show no coherent warm highlights or localized bounce.
Depth of field is too strong and/or focused incorrectly—no tack-sharp focal point on the flame core; macro intent fails.
Volumetric look is blotchy/low-frequency, suggesting insufficient volume sampling and/or over-aggressive denoising.
Composition/framing doesn’t guide the eye to a clear subject; the visible shapes don’t communicate ‘candle on desk’.
suggestions: Raise visibility first (debug pass): increase scene exposure or flame/emission intensity until the wick, candle rim, and flame silhouette are clearly readable in a single frame.
Fix DOF: set the focus plane on the flame core/wick and reduce blur so the flame core is crisp while background books fall into bokeh (not the entire subject).
Improve flame shading/colors: drive color by temperature/blackbody (blue-white at hottest inner core, then yellow/orange) and ensure flame is emissive enough to light nearby wax/brass.
Reduce smoke density drastically for a clean-burning candle; aim for delicate wisps. Then add higher-frequency detail (noise/vorticity) so smoke forms thin curling filaments, not a blob.
Increase volumetric sampling / reduce denoising blur to preserve fine smoke detail and avoid blotchy volume artifacts.
Recompose so the flame and top of candle occupy the visual center of interest; ensure at least the wick and a small portion of the holder are in-frame to convey scale.

Add/strengthen local light interaction: ensure the flame contributes visible warm highlights on brass and subtle subsurface-like glow on wax (even if approximated), plus gentle shadowing/contact lighting.
vision_assessment: The render reads as a very dark, heavily blurred scene with a couple of soft warm-brown smears; there is no clear, sharp candle flame, no visible wick, and no recognizable candle/holder detail. The intended macro candle-flame look (blue core, yellow/orange body, thin wispy smoke) is not present or not visible at the current exposure/DOF. As a result, the shot cannot be evaluated as a candle fire VFX and is far below production quality.
